title: Ramification multiplicity in the supported Cartier purity comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, $s\geq1$ and $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z$. Let $X,X'$ be Noetherian regular affine schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $g\in\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ be nonzerodivisors, and assume $D=V(f)$ and $D'=V(g)$ are regular. These are effective Cartier divisors [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Let $h:X'\to X$ satisfy $h^*f=g^e$ for an integer $e\geq1$. Write $i,i'$ for their closed inclusions, $j:X-D\hookrightarrow X$ and $j':X'-D'\hookrightarrow X'$ for the complementary opens, and $h_D:D'\to D$ for the induced map. Use ordinary small-etale derived module categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the finite Tate line $A(-1)$ dual to $\mu_{\ell^s}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], and the ordinary supported Kummer classes [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. Put
$$K_D=\operatorname{fib}(A_X\longrightarrow Rj_*A_{X-D}),\qquad K_{D'}=\operatorname{fib}(A_{X'}\longrightarrow Rj'_*A_{X'-D'}).$$
The supported Kummer classes factor uniquely through these fibres and give isomorphisms $P_D:i_*A_D(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_D$ and $P_{D'}:i'_*A_{D'}(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{D'}$. Let $\theta:h^*K_D\to K_{D'}$ be induced by the identity $h^*A_X=A_{X'}$ and the open direct-image exchange, i.e. the mate of the pullback square, with its actual unit normalization. Let $\rho:h^*i_*A_D(-1)\to i'_*A_{D'}(-1)$ be the closed exchange followed by reduction from $V(g^e)$ to $V(g)$ and the canonical Tate-line pullback. Then the following equality holds in $D(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$:
$$\theta\circ h^*P_D=P_{D'}\circ(e\,\rho)[-2].$$
In particular, the transition on the sole nonzero cohomology sheaf of the supported objects, in degree $2$, is $e$ times the closed Tate-line exchange. The formula includes empty divisors and $e=1$.

proof.text: Write $S_D=i_*A_D(-1)[-2]$ and let $q_D:K_D\to A_X$ be the fibre inclusion. The localization triangle is the actual counit/unit triangle of lem-exc-closed-support-triangle. For any bounded-below $M$ with $j^*M=0$, derived adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(M,Rj_*A_U[r])=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*M,A_U[r])=0$ for every integer $r$. Exactness of Hom into this triangle and its shifts therefore gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(M,K_D)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,A_X)$ induced by $q_D$. Apply this also on $X\prime$. For $M=S_D$ the support condition follows from closed-subtopos localization.

source.place: Section 2.1, supported class and forgetting support; Stacks 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle

proof.text: Put $N=\ell^s$. The roots-of-unity Tate sheaf is a locally free rank-one $A$-module. Tensoring the supported Kummer morphism $c_{D,A}:i_*A_D\to A_X(1)[2]$ by its dual line and shifting by $-2$ gives $a_D:S_D\to A_X$. Here the identification of its source with $i_*A_D(-1)$ is the adjunction projection map, an isomorphism on every geometric stalk (the identity evaluation on $D$, and zero off $D$). Step 1 gives its unique lift $P_D:S_D\to K_D$, characterized by $q_DP_D=a_D$. This constructs both lifts with the positive Kummer sign; no purity assertion is used for existence or uniqueness.

source.place: Sections 2.1 and 2.3: retype the ordinary supported Kummer class by the dual Tate line

proof.text: Each nonempty component of $D\hookrightarrow X$ is a regular immersion of codimension one: its ideal is generated by the nonzerodivisor $f$. Apply regular-pair purity with $c=1$, $n=s$ to obtain $A_D\simeq Ri^!A_X(1)[2]$. The class-calculus statement identifies its adjunction transpose with precisely $c_{D,A}$. Tensor by $A_D(-1)$, shift by $-2$, apply the exact $i_*$, and identify $i_*Ri^!A_X$ with $K_D$ through the counit/unit support triangle. The resulting map composes with $q_D$ to $a_D$, so Step 1 identifies it with $P_D$; hence $P_D$ is an isomorphism. Apply the same argument to $(X\prime,D\prime)$. For an empty divisor the closed object is zero and $j$ is the identity, so both objects are zero.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.1, printed p. 242 (PDF p. 248), codimension one; class normalization in Section 2.3

proof.text: Keep the scheme-theoretic pullback $E=X\prime\times_XD=V(g^e)$ distinct from $D\prime=V(g)$. Since $g^e$ is a nonzerodivisor, $E$ is Cartier. The immersion $r:D\prime\hookrightarrow E$ is a nilpotent thickening, and $E$ and $D\prime$ determine the same closed subtopos of $X\prime$ because their complementary opens agree. The closed-subtopos equivalence identifies their supported constant and Tate sheaves by the actual units and counits. The composite of closed exchange for the Cartesian $E$ square, restriction along $r$, and Tate pullback is exactly $\rho$. Pullback of the ordinary Cartier Kummer morphism across the Cartesian $E$ square is $c_{E,A}$, by the arbitrary-pullback clause of the supported Kummer statement. This application does not require $E$ to be regular.

source.place: Section 2.1: pullback of a framed pseudo-divisor; Stacks 08LY-08M1, closed subtopos with fixed complement

proof.text: For $E_k=V(g^k)$, the product ideal $(g^k)(g)=(g^{k+1})$ gives the tensor identity of Cartier lines with their canonical complement sections. Cartier pair tensor addition gives $\beta_{E_{k+1}}=\beta_{E_k}+\beta_{D\prime}$ after the canonical restriction of supported constants; all the closed supports here are the same closed subtopos. For $k=1$ the class is $\beta_{D\prime}$. Induction thus gives $\beta_E=e\beta_{D\prime}$. The same node states compatibility with the relative connecting maps, so applying the Kummer boundary and then scalar extension gives $c_{E,A}=e c_{D\prime,A}$ under the closed restriction. Tensoring by the negative Tate line and shifting consequently gives $h^*a_D=a_{D\prime}\circ(e\rho)[-2]$. This is additivity of the positive Kummer boundary and introduces no inverse of $e$.

source.place: Section 2.1, additive supported first Chern class of a tensor power; Stacks 03PL (lemma-kummer-sequence)

proof.text: The specified open exchange is the adjunction mate with its actual unit. Exact inverse image carries the fibre triangle to a triangle, and the induced fibre map $\theta$ satisfies $q_{D\prime}\theta=h^*q_D$. Therefore $q_{D\prime}\theta h^*P_D=h^*a_D=a_{D\prime}(e\rho)[-2]=q_{D\prime}P_{D\prime}(e\rho)[-2]$. The source $h^*S_D$ restricts to zero on $X\prime-D\prime$, since the inverse image of $X-D$ is $X\prime-D\prime$. Applying the bijectivity in Step 1 to this source cancels $q_{D\prime}$ and proves the asserted derived equality, with the specified mate rather than an unspecified scalar-normalized comparison.

source.place: Section 2.1 pullback of supported classes, combined with the actual unit triangle of Stacks 0A45

proof.text: The closed direct images of the Tate lines are sheaves in degree zero and are exact. Their shifts by $-2$ therefore have no cohomology outside degree $2$. Taking $H^2$ of the derived equality of Step 6 gives multiplication by $e$ followed by the specified closed Tate-line exchange. If $e=1$, this is precisely $\rho$; if $\ell^s\mid e$, it is zero without affecting either purity isomorphism. If either divisor is empty, its supported object is zero and the equality still holds. The phrase sole nonzero cohomology sheaf is read as only possibly nonzero cohomology sheaf, as required by the explicitly included empty case.

Source: ILO XVI Thm 3.1.1 (printed p.242, PDF p.248) covers any regular Z[1/n]-pair, with no smoothness or excellence hypothesis. Step checks: (1) support triangle, D^+ adjunction and Hom-exactness at two shifts give a bijection, not only a lift. (2) N=ℓ^s, NA=0, D Cartier, the dual twist line is locally free and the projection map is checked on stalks. (3) A nonzerodivisor on regular X gives codimension 1 with a length-one regular sequence; purity with c=1, n=s, and the equivalently-clause supplies the twist shift. The class-calculus c=1 clause fixes the positive Kummer transpose, so uniqueness identifies it with P_D. (4) E=V(g^e) is Cartier, which is all the pullback clause needs; it has the same closed subtopos as D', and support-Hom naturality gives the exchange ρ. (5) Explicit induction (g^k)(g)=(g^{k+1}) using tensor addition and its connecting-map and coefficient compatibility; no inverse of e. (6) θ is uniquely determined via Step 1 because h^*K_D is supported on D', then cancel q_{D'}. (7) Edge cases: e=1, ℓ^s|e, D empty, and D' empty with D nonempty. Small cases: t↦t^e on A^1, and Spec Z[1/ℓ] ⊃ V(p), which shows the regular-pair input is genuinely needed. Batch-5: lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction (homological algebra) and lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-localization (closed subtopos) are generic, are given by neither assumption, and are already in the base target closure, so both are accepted. All 10 tool_uses are accepted.
